nodes.label: CyberAlchemy
nodes.plain_language: The governed human-machine work product whose meaning this package serves.
nodes.claim: Registry Context contributes to the CyberAlchemy product by keeping source-backed meaning and work context connected for one bounded use.
nodes.scope: Projected product identity only.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a product realization, market claim, release, or runtime.

nodes.label: Governed Human-Machine Integration
nodes.plain_language: The committed CyberAlchemy product direction that Registry Context must support without becoming its owner.
nodes.claim: Bounded, source-current context supports shared meaning, evidence continuity, owner continuity, and honest incompleteness.
nodes.scope: Projected root Product Thesis node.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not accepted or proved by Registry Context validation.

nodes.label: CyberAlchemy v2 Define Project
nodes.plain_language: The proposed coordination boundary used by the first Registry Context example.
nodes.claim: The Define Project connects product meaning, the Define Goal, owners, evidence, and future runtime work under one stable identity.
nodes.scope: Projected proposed Project record.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Define owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Project membership grants no implementation or semantic authority.

nodes.label: Define First-Class Ownership Goal
nodes.plain_language: The draft desired result used by the first Registry Context example.
nodes.claim: The Goal seeks a source-backed owner-qualified Define contract while keeping separate authority lanes visible.
nodes.scope: Projected draft Goal record.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Define owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A context view cannot activate or achieve the Goal.

nodes.label: Define Shared Meaning
nodes.plain_language: The first consumer used to prove Registry Context composition.
nodes.claim: Define needs bounded Product, Project, Goal, Definition, and Language context before it can resolve or expose required meaning honestly.
nodes.scope: Projected Define product capability.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus Define runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an implemented Define runtime or accepted Definition Pack producer.

nodes.label: Resolve Bounded Language Context
nodes.plain_language: A Language-owned specialization that resolves the meanings and relationships needed for one use.
nodes.claim: Language Context resolution is the strongest current specialization pattern for generic Registry Context resolution.
nodes.scope: Projected Language product capability.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not replaced by the generic capability and not an accepted runtime.

nodes.label: Language Context View
nodes.plain_language: The Language-owned bounded view consumed by Define.
nodes.claim: A Registry Context View may include the exact Language Context View identity and bindings without absorbing Language ownership.
nodes.scope: Projected Language product output.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Language Project owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a generic Registry Context View and not proof that Define applied it correctly.

nodes.label: Registry
nodes.plain_language: An owner-controlled collection that makes typed records addressable for its declared scope.
nodes.claim: Registry Context reads named registries through their declared profiles and owners instead of treating repository proximity as membership.
nodes.scope: Package-local candidate concept used by Registry Context; not a canonical generic primitive.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus each registry owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a canonical Definition, event ledger, folder, or source of authority by membership.
open_questions: Does generic Registry later need canonical Definition authority, or should it remain a package-local concept?

nodes.label: Binding
nodes.plain_language: An explicit typed relationship between named endpoints with evidence, status, owner, and non-collapse limits.
nodes.claim: Registry Context includes only source-backed bindings and never derives one from shared labels or registry membership.
nodes.scope: Package-local candidate concept constrained by CAV2-D16.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus each binding owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an inferred equivalence, registry membership, owner decision, or authority transfer.

nodes.label: Registry Context Source Selection
nodes.plain_language: The exact source value and digest relied upon by one Registry Context resolution.
nodes.claim: Selection-level currency can fail closed for relevant meaning while treating unrelated containing-file change as diagnostic.
nodes.scope: JSON pointers, stable ID-selected JSON records, and exact Markdown H2 sections.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus each source owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a replacement source or a claim that the whole containing file is current.
open_questions: Should a later contract adopt a standard JSON canonicalization profile?

nodes.label: Registry Context Request
nodes.plain_language: One bounded request naming who needs context, why, and which exact registry selections may be used.
nodes.claim: A request prevents unbounded scans and makes required versus optional inputs explicit.
nodes.scope: One consumer, purpose, product/work scope, registry query set, currency policy, and binding policy.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an arbitrary path query, repository-wide search, prompt, or authority envelope.

nodes.label: Resolve Registry Context
nodes.plain_language: Build one small current context view from named registries and explicit bindings.
nodes.claim: The capability can give Define and later consumers the context they need without moving registry ownership or hiding unresolved differences.
nodes.scope: Read, select, validate, bind, project, and explain only.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a universal knowledge engine, source writer, owner decision, promotion mechanism, or implemented runtime.
open_questions: Which owner should accept the future runtime contract?

nodes.label: Registry Context View
nodes.plain_language: The immutable, digest-bound context bundle returned for one request.
nodes.claim: The view preserves included records, explicit bindings, exact source epoch, owners, residue, and its claim ceiling.
nodes.scope: One consumer and intended use only.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a source registry, event ledger, Definition Pack, or proof of correct use.

nodes.label: Registry Context Residue
nodes.plain_language: A visible unresolved condition found while resolving context.
nodes.claim: Missing, stale, ambiguous, conflicting, open, and owner-unresolved conditions remain typed and routed instead of being guessed away.
nodes.scope: Resolution-local unresolved state with evidence and owner route.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus the unresolved subject owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an automatically ignorable warning or an owner decision.

nodes.label: Preserve Registry Context Integrity
nodes.plain_language: Use only declared current selections and explicit bindings; expose everything else as residue or block.
nodes.claim: Registry Context must fail closed for changed required selections, dangling references, missing authority metadata, implicit bindings, or unbounded requests.
nodes.scope: Every Registry Context request, resolution, view, and explanation.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus affected source owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Validation PASS is not source promotion, context acceptance, or runtime conformance.

nodes.label: Registry Context Resolver
nodes.plain_language: The proposed read-only component that would execute Registry Context resolution.
nodes.claim: A deterministic resolver is a candidate realization of the business capability.
nodes.scope: Candidate system decomposition only.
nodes.owner_route: unresolved Registry Context runtime owner route
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an accepted Runtime Contract or implemented component.
open_questions: Who owns and accepts the Registry Context runtime contract?

nodes.label: Registry Adapter
nodes.plain_language: A module-owned reader that exposes one registry through the common resolution contract.
nodes.claim: Adapters let the shared resolver read Product, Language, Project, Goal, and Define records without taking their ownership.
nodes.scope: Read and project only; adapter semantics stay with each registry owner.
nodes.owner_route: each registry owner plus unresolved Registry Context runtime owner route
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a registry owner, writer, schema converter with promotion effect, or implicit binding engine.
open_questions: Which minimal adapter interface can cover the first four registries without premature generalization?

nodes.label: Registry Source Snapshot
nodes.plain_language: The exact selected values and digests observed for one resolution.
nodes.claim: A source snapshot can calculate a deterministic selection epoch without using a whole-repository clock.
nodes.scope: The selections declared by one request only.
nodes.owner_route: unresolved Registry Context runtime owner route plus each source owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not source authority, an event ledger, or proof that unrelated file content is current.

nodes.label: Registry Context Request Record
nodes.plain_language: The closed JSON record accepted by a future resolver.
nodes.claim: The candidate schema can represent one bounded exact request without arbitrary path input.
nodes.scope: The `$defs/contextRequest` contract in this package schema.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an accepted API, Runtime Contract, transport, or authority envelope.

nodes.label: Registry Context View Record
nodes.plain_language: The closed JSON projection produced for one request.
nodes.claim: The candidate schema preserves request identity, source epoch, records, explicit bindings, residue, view digest, and authority ceiling.
nodes.scope: The `$defs/contextView` contract in this package schema.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an accepted API, source registry, or proof of correct downstream use.

nodes.label: Registry Resolution Run Record
nodes.plain_language: A future append-only no-effect record of one resolution attempt.
nodes.claim: Run evidence may record inputs, result, source epoch, view digest, errors, and residue without becoming context truth.
nodes.scope: Deferred observability record only.
nodes.owner_route: unresolved Registry Context runtime owner route
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a source epoch, current view, owner decision, or authority event.
open_questions: Which run fields are needed after the read-only resolver exists?

nodes.label: Registry Resolution Ledger
nodes.plain_language: A future append-only sequence of Registry Resolution Run Records.
nodes.claim: If runtime audit becomes necessary, run records may use the CAV2-D26 pattern without turning the ledger into the current registry or view.
nodes.scope: Deferred run history only.
nodes.owner_route: unresolved Registry Context runtime owner route
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a Registry, source of current truth, source epoch, Product Thesis record, Project state, Goal state, or owner decision.
open_questions: Is a ledger needed after the initial deterministic CLI proof?
